pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: scripts/app-master-bench/gate.mjs:16 The regression verdict for each scenario comes from a single run (N=1). There are no repeated trials, no declared N and no measured variance (tolerance is a fixed fraction of each bar), so one noisy live night can pass or fail the gate, and the standard says a single run proves nothing in either direction.

techniques.evidence: scripts/app-master-bench/gate.mjs:16 Gate verdict is one run per scenario with no trial count attached. Within that run, gate.mjs:73 also takes the busiest night (a max over nights), which is an optimistic any-of-N style reduction reported without N.

scripts/app-master-bench/scenarios.mjs:338 Scenario identity is the name alone. Searching run.mjs, scenarios.mjs and gate.mjs for createHash/sha256/scenario version found nothing, so edits to a scenario file (e.g. kp-c1-night, Aug 31) are compared against a baseline recorded 2026-08-26 as if they were one series. The expected-properties half is realized: each scenario has an `expect` block, and kp-rung0.json:3 states its seeded stage.

scripts/app-master-bench/gate.mjs:27 Mock mode (--stub-personas) is marked on the record, the gate refuses stub runs with a `stub` verdict, and report.mjs:152 labels stub rows CANNED, so a mocked score never reaches a real trend.

scripts/app-master-bench/gate.mjs:297 The gate counts its failure families (missing/fail/stub/stale/unmetered/unbaselined) separately beside the pass count, and an unmeasured metric is a problem, never a zero (gate.mjs:120).

scripts/app-master-bench/expectations.mjs:359 Rank and decline checks are deterministic assertions. The part that needs taste (was a decline reason true) is explicitly left to a human spot-check rather than handed to a judge.

scripts/app-master-bench/gate.mjs:138 Each baselined metric is a threshold with a direction, declared once in baseline.json before the run. This is a pure regression gate, so it has no optimized metric to declare.

scripts/app-master-bench/expectations.mjs:12 No model judge anywhere in the bench: a grep for judge/rubric/pairwise/holdout in the non-test .mjs files found only a stub rationale string. Every check is a coded expectation.
